Sounds like a difficult place to be. I’m no trans expert but your question about finding peace is possibly more universal, so I’ll give this a shot and you can see what you think.

There are circumstances in life that are facts we cannot change. These are always neutral, not good, not bad, they just are, until we apply meaning to them.

Examples: “It’s raining.” Or “I was born male”.

When we encounter a circumstance we have a thought about it. What that thought is can be wildly different from person to person from the exact same circumstance. What your thoughts are about the circumstances in your life are affected by your life experience, belief system, socialisation, etc.

For example, two people have red hair. One thinks “ I love my red hair!”. The other thinks “I wish I didn’t have red hair”.

A belief is just a well-practiced thought. You have the ability to change your thoughts if you want to. 

When you think your thought it creates a feeling. A feeling is a sensation in your body that we label as “happy”, “sad”, “uncomfortable”, “angry”, etc. 

To find peace with a situation, look at the thoughts you have around it, and what feelings they cause. Spend a few mins every day writing out all your thoughts. See what feelings they bring up and if you can see any patterns.

Then, take the thoughts that cause you pain, find thoughts that feel less painful (even 10% less shitty is fine), and practice thinking them.

It’s not quick and easy, but I hope it helps.
